Air Response Unit: Solid role-player, not a bomb. A crew-1 3/3 flyer with vigilance is easy to turn on and its 51% GIH / -1.6 IWD say it's a fine finisher that mostly comes down late, not a card that swings games. Best in WU vehicles/RW beatdown where the evasion helps chip toward Max Speed.
Alacrian Armory: Filler-to-sideboard. A 4-mana anthem that only shines with a dense Mount/Vehicle base, but the 46.5% GIH WR and negative IWD confirm the D+ grade — it does nothing the turn it lands and this slow format punishes do-nothing enchantments. Only in a committed RW vehicles shell, and even then it's late.
Basri, Tomorrow's Champion: Solid playable one-drop rare that never rots: a 2/1 that pumps out lifelink Cats, and if it's late you cycle it for a card plus a combat trick. The 57.3% GIH / 61.9% OH backs the B — a flexible early play that scales into a token engine for any white deck, best in a go-wide Big White or WG shell.
Brightfield Glider: Filler one-drop that only matters in a saddle-heavy RW/GW shell. As a 1/1 vigilance it's below replacement, but saddled it's a +1/+2 flyer that pushes evasive damage. The 52.7% GIH sits near the floor with a negative IWD — a role-player you play when your Mounts deck needs bodies, not a pick.
Brightfield Mustang: Filler at best. A 3/3 for four that only grows if you spend other creatures to saddle it, and the sub-50% GIH WR plus negative IWD confirm it does nothing on an empty board. In a slow format a vanilla-ish four-drop that needs support is below replacement; last pick over any real card.
Broadcast Rambler: Solid playable and the backbone of Big White. Six total power across two bodies (5/4 vehicle plus a 1/1 flyer) for five mana lets white contest green's fatties and crews itself. 56.1% GIH beats the timid C grade; LoL calls it wildly underrated. Prioritize in W midrange.
Bulwark Ox: Solid early playable, not a bomb despite the rare stamp. It's a 2/2 for 2, which the format punishes, but saddle-1 is cheap and it grows your team while giving a hexproof/indestructible protection button; 55.4% GIH and 58% OH earn its B. Best in counters/Mount decks (WG, RW).
Canyon Vaulter: Role-player, not a slam. A 3/1 body is fragile and the flying-grant only fires when it saddles/crews on your main phase, so it's an RW/vehicles enabler that turns your Mount into an evasive Max-Speed finisher. The 54.6% GIH is honest for a 2-drop but the C+ grade is right: playable glue in the vehicle shell, cuttable elsewhere.
Cloudspire Captain: Role-player, only worth it in RW/WU vehicles. A 2/3 anthem-plus-crew-booster whose 51.8% GIH and negative IWD confirm it does nothing outside a real vehicle/Mount critical mass. B- grade is the ceiling in Boros; a filler body if your deck lacks payloads to crew.
Collision Course: Flexible filler. Mode one is a Fireball scaled to your board width, mode two spot-removes an artifact/vehicle, so it's never fully dead. The 53.9% GIH and +0.2 IWD say it's a fine late-deck inclusion in a wide creature deck, not a card you prioritize; take real removal or bodies first.
Daring Mechanic: Filler. A 3/3 for three clears Scotty's power/toughness bar but the {3}{W} counter sink is expensive and only lives in the RW/WU vehicle shells, and even there it's a slow do-nothing. The 51% GIH and negative IWD confirm the C-: a body you play when the deck is thin, not a card you want.
Detention Chariot: Solid playable, near-premium white removal. A 6/6 body that exiles any opponent artifact or creature on ETB, with cycling {W} so it's never dead when you're stuck. The 55.9% GIH and early 3.5 ALSA beat its cautious C+; the flexible answer plus a huge crew-3 clock is exactly what grindy Big White wants, and it doubles as a Push the Limit cycling O-Ring.
Gallant Strike: Solid conditional removal — better than its C grade. The toughness-4-or-greater clause is aimed exactly at the 4-toughness bodies that define this slow format, and cycling {2} means it's never a dead card, hence the 57% GIH and +2.2 IWD off an 85% play rate. Reliable white two-drop answer.
Gloryheath Lynx: Solid early playable, take it. A 2/3 lifelinker for two dodges the vanilla-2/2 trap (3 toughness) and the saddle-tutor smooths mana; 59.6% GIH with a huge +5.4 IWD and 3.0 ALSA back the B grade. The 63.3% OH WR means it's happy in your opener, not a synergy card — good in any white deck.
Guardian Sunmare: Bomb-adjacent Mount and a first-pick — a 5/5 Ward 2 body that, once saddled, tutors any 3-drop permanent straight onto the battlefield every attack. 58.7% GIH with a huge +6.3 IWD confirms the B undersells it; Saddle 4 is trivial to turn on and the free bodies snowball. Slam it in any white deck, elite in WG.
Guidelight Synergist: Solid artifact-deck role-player and a great blocker in the slow format. A 0/4 flyer is a wall that grows with each artifact you control, going over the top in UB/artifact affinity. The 55.1% GIH and +2.5 IWD beat its pessimistic C- grade — the 4-toughness flyer body earns its keep even outside a dedicated artifact deck.
Interface Ace: Role-player for RW/WU vehicle-pilot shells only. A 0/4 body that crews and saddles off toughness and re-untaps once per turn is a great enabler, but the 49% WR shows it's dead weight outside a deck with enough Vehicles/Mounts to enable. Take it late as glue, not a playable on its own.
Leonin Surveyor: Filler two-drop that overperforms its stats because of the graveyard draw. A 2/2 first striker on your turn is a below-replacement body in this slow format, but max-speed card draw gives it a late-game floor. Negative IWD (-1.8) confirms it's a curve-filler, not a pick you reach for.
Lightshield Parry: Filler combat trick with an escape hatch. +2/+2 for {W} is fine but negative IWD (-2.8) confirms tricks lag in this slow, grindy format; the cycling {2} is why it's playable at all — never a dead card. Sideboard/23rd-card, not a maindeck priority.
Lightwheel Enhancements: Filler-to-sideboard Aura. A one-mana +1/+1 vigilance with graveyard recursion at max speed, but it's still a two-for-one risk that does nothing to the board. The 48.6% GIH and ugly -3.9 IWD confirm the D+; only take it late as a curve-filler in an aggressive white deck.
Lotusguard Disciple: Solid combat-trick-on-a-body playable, best in WU/WB. A 2/2 flyer is below the 3-power/3-toughness bar, but the lifelink+indestructible ETB blanks removal or wins a fight, and the 53.0% GIH beats its C grade. Card is fine, the flimsy body isn't.
Nesting Bot: Trap despite the 55.9% GIH and 58.5% OH. The one-drop 1/1 wanted an aggressive white shell that DFT never supported — LoL's retro is blunt: "basically a blank piece of cardboard," white was big-midrange not weenie-aggro. The WR is a mirage from early-format white-aggro experiments; leave it for the sideboard and draft big white instead.
Perilous Snare: Premium removal — one of the best reasons to be in white. A {2}{W} O-Ring that exiles any nonland permanent (creature, vehicle, artifact, enchantment) answers this grindy format's biggest threats, and the max-speed counter mode is pure upside. The 62% GIH, +9.1 IWD, and 1.6 ALSA blow past the modest B grade; take it very early.
Pride of the Road: Filler defensive body. A 2/5 vigilance blocks the format's midsize creatures well, but its max-speed double-strike payoff is awkward in slow white, which turns speed on poorly. The negative IWD and 52.2% GIH match the D+ read: a fine roleplayer in Big White that never swings a game. Take real cards over it.
Ride's End: Premium common removal and the reason to be in white — take it high. Instant-speed exile for effectively {1}{W} against anything tapped (attackers, crewed Vehicles, Mounts) answers even Migrating Ketradon and is splashable. The 57.3% GIH / +3.4 IWD undersell it since removal doesn't win from hand; LoL: 'all hail Ride's End.'
Roadside Assistance: Role-player, mid-pick. The Pilot token is the real payoff — it crews Vehicles and saddles Mounts for cheap, so it props up an RW/WU vehicle shell; the +1/+1 lifelink aura is upside. But 53.1% GIH with a flat -0.3 IWD says it's replaceable filler outside a Mount/Vehicle-heavy build. Grade B- is generous.
Salvation Engine: First-pick bomb in the artifact decks. A 6/10 wall that anthem-buffs your artifact creatures and reanimates an artifact each attack — Crew 6 looks steep but the body blocks everything and the value is inevitable. 55.1% GIH understates it because it's a build-around (LoL: grossly powerful, take late in big white/UB affinity). Trust the ceiling, not the raw number.
Skyseer's Chariot: A premium two-drop vehicle — 3/3 flyer for two, crew 2, that also taxes an opponent's key activated ability. Aggressively costed evasion is exactly what this grindy format lacks, and the 54.7% GIH with a top-tier 3.3 ALSA and 70%+ play rate confirm the B grade. First-pickable in any deck that can crew it.
Spectacular Pileup: Premium bomb and a top-end white pick. A cycling board wipe that even blanks indestructible — the doctrine's marquee white card: 55.8% GIH, +3.0 IWD and an A grade all agree, and because nobody fights you for white you can wheel it. Cycling means it's never dead in the fast matchups. Grab it every time.
Spotcycle Scouter: Role-player curve piece. A 3/2 crew-1 vehicle with scry 2 smooths draws and pressures early, but 22% play rate and negative IWD say it's a fringe inclusion, not a staple. Fine early-turn body in WU/vehicle shells; don't overvalue the LoL 'excellent curve play' preview hype.
Sundial, Dawn Tyrant: Efficient role-player: a 3/3 for 2 with 3 toughness clears Scotty's two-drop bar and blocks the format's relevant bodies. Vanilla but on-rate; 55.3% GIH and 82% play back the B-. Good filler in any white deck, never exciting — take real cards over it.
Swiftwing Assailant: Playable role-player. A 3/3 flyer for four is fine evasion in a slow format, and max speed bumps it to 3/4 vigilance so it attacks and blocks. The 53.2% GIH beats its C- grade; solid filler that any deck wanting air can run, but nothing to prioritize.
Tune Up: Filler/build-around, only for UR cycling. A slow reanimation sorcery that combos with Push the Limit (cycle a bomb vehicle, return it turn 4), but a 34% play rate and D grade say it's a niche 23rd card. The +1.0 IWD is the enabled deck talking; provisional value elsewhere.
Unswerving Sloth: Below-rate role-player. A five-mana 5/5 with no ETB is a real knock in this grindy format; the saddle-4 indestructible-plus-untap-all payoff needs a wide RW/WG board to matter and rarely shows up. 52.9% GIH and negative IWD confirm the guides' retro tone-down — a curve-topper only when you're short on bodies.
Valor's Flagship: Bomb, and flexible. A 7/7 flying first-strike lifelink vehicle for six that ends games when crewed, but its real strength is the cycling-for-X mode that makes Pilot tokens when you're flooded or stuck — never a dead card. 56% GIH understates it because it's often cycled 'late'; the token pilots make it an all-star in RW/vehicle and Push the Limit builds.
Voyager Glidecar: Strong early pick and slam-quality one-drop. A {W} 2/3 that scries on ETB, then converts to an evasive attacker with a growing counter — the rare vehicle that's live on turn one and scales late. 56.3% GIH, +3.5 IWD and 2.6 ALSA back the B+; excellent glue for any white deck, especially WU/vehicles.
Voyager Quickwelder: Playable body that's better in artifact decks (UB affinity, WU). A 2/4 for three blocks the format's relevant creatures and the {1}-off artifact discount is real gravy, not a build-around; 55% GIH with a modest play rate says it's a fine early pick that shines when your deck is artifact-dense.
Aether Syphon: Playable value engine that beats its D- grade badly — 55.9% GIH and +3.6 IWD at 70.7% play say the market corrected the theory. Repeatable card draw for {2} is exactly what a slow grindy format wants, and the mill is incidental; take it as a UB/UR card-advantage piece, not the mill payoff the name implies.
Bounce Off: Premium blue tempo interaction and a high pick — one mana to bounce anything, including a vehicle mid-crew for free. LoL's late read reframes it: it's about patience in this slow format, saving your bomb or resetting a key turn, not raw tempo. 55.9% GIH with a late 5.9 ALSA means it wheels; always-playable UB/UR glue.
Caelorna, Coral Tyrant: A defensive specialist, not a threat — a 0/8 for two that hard-walls green fatties and the format's ground creatures. The 53.6% GIH is respectable for a card that does nothing but block, and it buys the long game blue support decks want. Fine role-player in UB/UR control, unexciting in any deck with a clock.
Diversion Unit: Solid playable, borderline premium for UB/UR artifact decks. A 2/1 flier for two that later sacs to Force Spike is real tempo plus an evasive body and an artifact for affinity payoffs; 55.9% GIH and 89% play rate outrun the B- grade. First-pick-quality glue in blue.
Flood the Engine: Sneaky-good blue removal-lite at a 89.6% play rate. Permanently taps down and strips abilities from any creature or Vehicle — a hard answer to green's fatties and crewed threats in a slow grind. 56.2% GIH and +1.9 IWD blow past the C grade; a genuine Ux staple.
Gearseeker Serpent: Payoff finisher for artifact/affinity decks. Base {5}{U}{U} 5/6 is clunky, but affinity makes it land early in UB and the {5}{U} unblockable pushes damage in a stall; the 54.7% drawn WR is conditioned on the artifact shell. Mid pick that gets much better in UB affinity.
Glitch Ghost Surveyor: Filler flyer. A 2/2 evasive body for three that only pays off once you hit max speed and can spend {3} to cash it from the yard for a card. The 51.2% GIH matches its C: replacement-level early game with a tiny late upside, fine as a 22nd-23rd card.
Guidelight Optimizer: Reliable UB/artifact playable. A 2/1 for two that also ramps into artifact spells and abilities — the affinity engines' mana rock with legs. 54.3% GIH and 69.5% play rate clear its C grade; take it when your deck is artifact-dense, otherwise a below-rate 2/1.
Howler's Heavy: Solid role-player and a cycling-deck sweetener. A 3/4 body is fine on the slow-format curve, but the value is the -3/-0 on cycle — a combat blowout that fuels UR discard-matters (Push the Limit). 55.0% GIH with +1.7 IWD reflects the flexibility; it's never a dead draw. Good early-mid pick in any blue deck.
Hulldrifter: Solid playable, best in UB/UR artifact decks. Draw two on ETB makes it card-neutral flying value even if you never crew the 3/2, so it's low-risk in any deck with bodies to tap. 55% GIH and +2.5 IWD back the C+; a fine mid-pick that flies over a stalled board.
Keen Buccaneer: Solid playable and a fine blue two-drop despite the vanilla-adjacent frame. The 2/3 body dodges the poorly-positioned 2/2 trap, and its exhaust loot + counter is a clean mana sink that smooths draws in any blue deck. 55.2% GIH and 78% play blow past the pessimistic C-; LoL's retro verdict is simply 'a good card.'
Memory Guardian: Strong affinity payoff — trust the live number over the C-implied ceiling. Affinity routinely makes this a 3/4 flyer for two or three mana, and 56.3% GIH with a huge +4.7 IWD confirms it overperforms in the UB artifact deck. Prioritize once you're committed to artifacts; mediocre in a low-artifact build.
Midnight Mangler: Fine early playable but nothing special. The 'iconic 2-mana 3/3' — and it blocks on their turn for free without crewing, which matters — but 54.1% GIH and +0.8 IWD peg it as a competent common, not a driver. Good curve filler for UB affinity/tempo; don't take it over removal or a real threat.
Mindspring Merfolk: Strong rare and an early pick — a one-mana body that becomes a repeatable {X}{U}{U} draw engine via exhaust, refueling grindy games perfectly for this slow format. 59.5% GIH and +6.6 IWD blow past the B: cheap to deploy, scales to a game-winning draw spell late. Any blue deck wants it, doubly so UB control.
Mu Yanling, Wind Rider: Bomb — first-pick, near-splashable mythic. She makes a flying vehicle token immediately, gives all your vehicles flying, and turns evasive damage into a card-draw engine. The 65.3% GIH, +13.4 IWD and 1.4 ALSA are among the best numbers in the set; take her over almost anything and go blue.
Nimble Thopterist: Solid playable. A 3/2 that leaves a 1/1 flying Thopter behind is two bodies for four, feeding UB artifact/affinity and thopter-token synergies; 55.4% GIH and low IWD say it's a reliable value common, not a bomb. Good early pick in any blue deck.
Possession Engine: Bomb. A five-mana Threaten-that-sticks: steal the opponent's best creature for as long as this 5/5 vehicle lives, swinging the board by two bodies. Elite 60.3% GIH, +8.1 IWD, 1.8 ALSA — take it over almost anything. Crew 3 is trivial once you've stolen a body.
Rangers' Refueler: Premium blue uncommon — a build-around engine, take it high. A {1}{U} 3/3 crew-2 vehicle that draws when you fire ANY exhaust ability, and it self-enables via its own exhaust; +5.1 IWD and 59.3% GIH are elite. Snowballs UB/GU exhaust decks; even standalone it's a fine early body.
Repurposing Bay: Trap/sideboard despite the rare stamp. It's a slow, sorcery-speed artifact tutor-chain that needs a dense artifact deck and does nothing the turn it lands; the 46.7% GIH and D- grade agree. Skip it in normal drafts; only a dedicated UB/artifact build wants this engine.
Riverchurn Monument: Premium, a top-pick despite the joke D- grade. This is CGB whiffing hard: the 60.0% GIH, +7.6 IWD, and 3.0 ALSA mark it as a real UB win condition — repeatable mill plus a devastating exhaust that decks the opponent while your control shell grinds. Trust the numbers, take it early.
Roadside Blowout: Premium blue interaction — take it highly. Bounce-plus-draw is card-neutral tempo, kills a vehicle mid-crew, and costs just {U} against a MV-1 target. LoL calls it "bread and butter for every blue deck" and the 82.8% play rate, 56.3% GIH, B grade all agree. One of blue's best support pieces.
Sabotage Strategist: Strong role-player for blue-based control. Flying vigilance on a 2/2 plus a repeatable -1/-0 to all attackers makes it a great defensive blocker in this slow format, and the exhaust turns it into a 5/5 late. 54.8% GIH with an early 3.7 ALSA supports the B; a reliable pick for UB/UR/WU.
Scrounging Skyray: Solid playable, and better in the right shell. A 1/2 flyer that grows off every discard, so it's an evasive win-con in UR/UB cycling-and-discard while still cycling {2} itself when you're not synergized. The excellent +5.1 IWD and 56.4% GIH beat its C+; prioritize it when you're leaning discard-matters.
Skystreak Engineer: Above-replacement two-drop despite the C- grade — it clears Scotty's bar with 3 toughness and evasion. A 1/3 flyer for {1}{U} chips damage and blocks early, then the exhaust turns it into a real threat late; 55.7% GIH / +2.0 IWD is a genuinely good common. Fine in any blue deck, best where exhaust matters (GU).
Slick Imitator: Filler. A 1/3 for two that only does anything at max speed, and even then the sac-to-copy ability is narrow and clunky in a slow format that struggles to hit max speed. 52.3% GIH and +0.2 IWD confirm the D+ read — it's a body that blocks. Fringe UR/BR spell decks only.
Spectral Interference: Underdrafted sideboard-to-maindeck gem, especially maindeckable given how green defines the format. A soft counter (pay 4) that stops Hazard, Keron, or any bomb on curve — LoL flags it as excellent versus green. 56.2% GIH beats the C- grade; a 6.3 ALSA means it's a free late pick for any UB/UR deck that fears big green.
Spell Pierce: Sideboard/niche card in a grindy Limited format — a soft counter that only hits noncreature spells and gets paid through in the late game. The sub-50% GIH and 8% play rate confirm it's near-unplayable maindeck; board it in against key removal or a build-around. Not a pick outside a heavy UR control seat.
Spikeshell Harrier: Elite uncommon — likely the best in the set (Ben's pick). A 4/4 for five that bounces a creature/Vehicle AND slows the racer's speed is pure tempo on a body that blocks everything; 59.4% GIH, +5.8 IWD, 92% play rate crush the B grade. Take it over most rares; the reason blue is a premier support color.
Stall Out: Sideboard-adjacent filler. Three stun counters is a slow, temporary tap that doesn't kill anything in a grindy format, though cycling keeps it from being dead. Sub-50% GIH and awful 45.6% OH_WR confirm the D+ grade; only run it when short on playables.
Stock Up: Premium blue common — near-first-pickable, take it over most creatures. Dig-3-of-5-keep-2 for {2}{U} is the best card selection in the set; the initial "garbage in a fast format" read fully reversed since DFT is slow. 59.5% GIH and +5.6 IWD; a staple in every blue deck.
Thopter Fabricator: Premium first-pick, effectively a bomb. A 4/4 flyer for three at crew 2 is already above rate, and the draw-two trigger spits out flyers in any deck that loots or cycles — elite in UR/UB. The 59.6% GIH, +8.4 IWD and 1.9 ALSA all scream slam; take it over almost anything.
Trade the Helm: Situational uncommon, best in UB/artifact control. A five-mana Control Magic swap that steals their bomb (or trades your token for it) and cycles when dead — the cycling floor is why the 51.7% GIH holds. Clunky and reactive; a fine playable, not a priority.
Transit Mage: High pick and the glue of UR artifacts. The +5.0 IWD and 59.0% GIH are elite for a 2/2 because it tutors your best 4-5 drop (Clamorous Ironclad, Boom Mobile) and consistently assembles Push the Limit. The body is irrelevant; you're paying for library consistency. CGB's C+ undersells it — trust the live numbers.
Trip Up: Role-player tempo/interaction. Bouncing to top OR bottom of library is soft removal — good against bombs and vehicles mid-crew — and cycling {2} means it's never dead. 54.5% GIH and a middling 51% play rate mark it as flexible filler; fine in any blue deck but not a high pick.
Unstoppable Plan: Trap/sideboard. A do-nothing enchantment with no immediate board impact; untapping your permanents each end step needs a built engine this slow format doesn't reliably provide. The 37.9% GIH, -3.3 IWD and 3.3% play rate confirm the F — it's essentially unplayable in Limited, so leave it in the box.
Vnwxt, Verbose Host: Trap-adjacent rare — the D grade is right and the 53.5% GIH barely clears water. A 0/4 that does nothing the turn it lands and only pays off at Max Speed, which blue decks reach unreliably, is a slow engine in a slow format. Playable filler in a controlling UB/UR draw-two shell, not an early pick.
Waxen Shapethief: Provisional-ish rare that plays as a role-player, not a bomb. Flash-clone-anything has a high ceiling but a 0/0 floor, and cycling {2} means it's never dead — that flexibility drives the 80.2% play and 2.8 ALSA. But 52.7% GIH matches the C grade; it copies your best thing or cycles, solid but unexciting. Take it, don't hype it.
Ancient Vendetta: Trap/sideboard filler — a narrow four-mana Cranial Extraction that does nothing to the board in a grindy creature format. Null WR with a 0.2% play rate and F grade tell the whole story; only touch it as a Bo3 hate card, never maindeck. Read is provisional given no data, but the ceiling is nonexistent.
Back on Track: Strong UB/BG value engine and a clear playable. For five it reanimates any creature or vehicle AND leaves a 1/1 pilot that crews/saddles as power 3 — so it's a two-for-one that fixes your crew problem too. LoL rates it above Tune Up for flexibility; the 57.8% GIH and +3.0 IWD back a grade higher than its B-.
Bloodghast: Trap in this slow format. The recursion needs constant landfall and it can't block, so on a stalled board it's a 2/1 that whiffs — the -4.4 IWD and sub-49% WR are damning. Aggro doesn't turn on the haste clause reliably; leave the reanimated hype at the door and take a body that blocks.
Carrion Cruiser: Strong BG/UB playable — a 3/2 crew-1 vehicle that mills two and rebuys your best creature or Vehicle for real card advantage. Feeds graveyard value and refuels the grind. 56.9% GIH and 3.7 ALSA back the B grade; a reliable early pick in the S-tier BG deck.
Chitin Gravestalker: Playable graveyard payoff, not a priority. A {5}{B} 5/4 that shrinks in the mill/self-fill decks, with cycling as the floor so it's never dead. Flat 53.7% GIH and 0 IWD peg it as replacement-level; take it as a curve-topper in UB/BG grindy decks, not a signal.
Cryptcaller Chariot: Strong early pick. A 5/5 menace for four at crew 2 is a beating on its own, and it snowballs hard in any discard/cycling deck (UR/UB), spawning tapped zombies every time you pitch. The 51.9% GIH under-sells it because it wants a discard shell; the +1.7 IWD and B+ grade are the truer read.
Cursecloth Wrappings: Strong build-around rare for WB/aristocrats. The 58.9% GIH, +5.2 IWD, and 2.2 ALSA reflect a repeatable embalm engine that rebuys your best dead creatures every turn plus a Zombie anthem. C grade undersells a grindy value machine; premium in the graveyard decks, mediocre without bodies to recur.
Deathless Pilot: Role-player for vehicle/mount decks (RW). It crews and saddles as a 4-power body and recurs itself from the yard, so it's a reliable enabler that never runs out. The note's "surveil" blurb is wrong — read the card. 53.6% GIH and -1.4 IWD say it's a support piece, valuable only when you actually have vehicles to crew.
Demonic Junker: Premium removal on a body. Affinity routinely casts this 4/3 for far less than {6}{B}, and the ETB is a two-sided Murder that grows the vehicle to a 6/5 when it eats your own creature — huge in UB/BG artifact decks. 90% play rate, 2.0 ALSA and +3.4 IWD earn the B+; take it early.
Engine Rat: Solid playable that overperforms its stats. A one-mana deathtouch 1/1 trades up against anything, blocks big green all day, and the {5}{B} drain becomes real reach in the grindy late game. 57.8% GIH and +2.7 IWD justify LoL's on-air apology ('you're a very good card'); a fine early black playable, not just filler.
Gas Guzzler: Fine aggressive one-drop, not the bomb 'rare' implies. A 2/1 that enters tapped is a mediocre body, and the sac-for-cards engine only unlocks at Max Speed — so the strong 59.7% OH_WR reflects it as a cheap curve-filler, while the 54% drawn WR shows it's weak in the late game. Best in BR/BG aggro where you have fodder.
Gastal Raider: Solid aggressive playable, high pick in BR. A 2/1 that strips an instant/sorcery on ETB and becomes a 3/2 menace at max speed — real disruption plus evasion. 55.4% GIH with 4.0 ALSA and 80% play backs the B-; the discard is a Momentum-Breaker-style tempo swing. Best when Start Your Engines is online, i.e. BR aggro.
Gonti, Night Minister: Strong midrange rare and a high pick — a 3/4 for four that blocks the format well and generates card advantage whenever your creatures connect, exiling from the opponent's deck. 57.9% GIH and a 91% play rate confirm it's a reliable engine above the B-; the Treasure clause rarely matters. Great in any black deck, best in grindy BG/UB.
Grim Bauble: Premium-adjacent black common — the reason black is in every deck. A one-mana -2/-2 that answers the format's problematic two-drops and 2/2s at instant speed on ETB, then later sacs for Surveil 2. The 57.5% GIH with 87.8% play rate and near-top ALSA make it a high pick; the -2/-2 is soft removal but the tempo and flexibility are elite.
Grim Javelineer: Role-player for aggressive black/BR. The attack trigger pumps a creature and surveils on trades, rewarding a wide, attacking board; 54.4% GIH but flat IWD says it needs the aggressive shell to shine. Fine playable in BR, mediocre in a grindy BG. Mid pick.
Hellish Sideswipe: Efficient one-mana removal that punches above the C+ grade — a Bone Splinters that kills any creature or Vehicle, and refunds a card if you sac a Vehicle. The sac cost wants a token/artifact deck to be free (WB, BG, UB). 54.4% GIH; premium-adjacent when you have fodder.
Hour of Victory: Strong Start-Your-Engines payoff, take it high in speed decks. Three mana for a 2/2 zombie is below rate on its own, but at max speed it becomes a repeatable Demonic Tutor for your best card. 55.1% GIH; premier BR/WB SYE engine — much weaker outside a speed shell.
Intimidation Tactics: Solid playable, better than its C-. A one-mana hand-strip that exiles their best creature or artifact with information, and cycles when dead — flexible interaction that's never a stone brick. The 54.9% GIH and +0.3 IWD reward it; a fine early-to-mid pick in black, especially the control mirrors.
Kalakscion, Hunger Tyrant: Filler beater, a trap over real cards. A 7/2 for three with no evasion or text dies to any block, chump, or 2-power trade in this slow format — glass-cannon stats. The flat 52.1% GIH and negative IWD confirm it: playable in aggressive black, but don't overrate the power number.
The Last Ride: Filler mythic that plays as a card-draw engine, not a beater — the 13/13 shrinks by your life total so it's usually a 0/0 you never attack with. The 2.7 ALSA shows people first-pick the shiny rarity then get a mediocre {2}{B}, pay-2-life draw outlet. 52.8% GIH is replacement-level; it's a fine one-drop looter, nothing more.
Locust Spray: Situational role-player. A one-mana -1/-1 that cycles for {B} — it kills X/1s and shrinks a blocker to push damage, and being a free cantrip when dead keeps it always-playable. The 53% GIH and thin 37% play rate say it's a flex slot, best in aggressive BR/WB where every point of reach matters.
Maximum Overdrive: Solid playable — one of the format's best combat tricks. +1/+1 with deathtouch and indestructible lets you attack or block profitably into the big green fatties that define DFT, winning any fight for cheap. 56.2% GIH and the LoL retro praise clear the timid C-; a two-way trick that shines in a slow, creature-combat format.
Momentum Breaker: Premium in BR, playable in most black decks — trust it over the D+ grade. The 56.7% GIH badly undersells the linchpin edict that enables a Start-Your-Engines turn and drains; LoL flags it needs aggressive trading so you don't hit tokens. Prioritize as the BR/WB aristocrats glue; a strong role-player elsewhere.
Mutant Surveyor: Best of the surveyor cycle — take it as a core BG/black common. A 2/3 that pumps to a 4/5 attacker for {2} and cashes itself for a card from the yard late; LoL ranks it #1 of the five 'by a large margin,' unblockable-feeling in the grind. 54.5% GIH slightly undersells it because the value is a late mana sink, not an opener.
Pactdoll Terror: Solid playable and a build-around payoff — a 3/4 for four is already a fine body in a 4-toughness format, and every artifact you play drains 1 and gains 1, which snowballs in affinity. 57.5% GIH and +4.2 IWD far exceed the C-: the number is conditioned on the UB artifact deck (combos with Haunt the Network). Prioritize it there.
Quag Feast: Premium black removal — a two-mana kill spell for creatures, planeswalkers, or vehicles that scales as your graveyard fills, hitting nearly everything in a slow format by midgame. The 58.1% GIH, +3.7 IWD and excellent 2.3 ALSA outrun its cautious B-; the self-mill even feeds BG graveyard payoffs. First-pick-quality removal in any black deck.
Ripclaw Wrangler: Filler. A 4/3 Crew-2 Vehicle whose one-time discard ETB is minor, and the tiny 16% play rate says most decks can't reliably crew it — a dead card without creatures to tap. The 51.6% WR comes from the few decks built to crew; don't prioritize it over real threats.
Risen Necroregent: Better than its D+ grade suggests — 53.9% GIH and 3.4 ALSA show it plays fine. A 5/4 for five that spits out a 2/2 each turn at max speed is a real threat, but max speed is the catch: it's a slow engine, not a beater, best in BR/WB decks that reliably rev up.
Risky Shortcut: Role-player card draw with real symmetry cost. Draw two for {2}{B} is efficient, but the 2 life to EACH player can help opponents' races and hurt you when behind; modest 35.8% play rate shows it's not universally wanted. Best in BR aggro where the drain is upside, filler elsewhere.
Shefet Archfiend: Premium — a wrath on a flyer. A 5/5 flyer that ETBs -2/-2 to the board swings most stalls, and cycling {2} means it's never dead early. The 55.1% GIH and B- undersell how often this just wins the grindy midgame; take it highly in any black deck.
The Speed Demon: Bomb, first-pick it. A 5/5 flying trample for five that draws you X cards at max speed is a game-ender that also has evasion to close — the 60.4% GIH, +6.7 IWD, and 1.6 ALSA are elite and blow past the cautious B- grade. Anchor of any black deck, best in BR/BG where speed comes online fast.
Spin Out: Premium removal — near the top of any black deck's picks. Unconditional destroy-creature-or-vehicle at instant speed is exactly the answer this grindy format wants, especially against big green. LoL: rare praise for a "murder variant." The 91.4% play rate and +2.7 IWD say auto-include; the C+ grade badly underrates it. Pull toward black.
Streaking Oilgorger: Filler that overperforms its grade. A 3/3 flyer with haste for five is unexciting, but evasion still matters in a slow format and max-speed lifelink helps you stabilize. 54.1% GIH beats the D+ — decode it as an aggressive-deck card (BR) whose damage helps turn on its own max speed; a fine late-curve flyer, not a priority.
Syphon Fuel: Solid removal, format-warped upward. -6/-6 kills nearly everything including 4-toughness bodies and the big green threats, plus 2 life matters in a grind; the {4}{B} cost is the only knock. 54.5% GIH with a strong 56.8% drawn beats the C-; the sorcery-speed-feeling instant is exactly the answer black wants.
Wickerfolk Indomitable: Below-replacement filler — the D grade and 50.4% GIH / -2.6 IWD agree. A 4/3 for four is a weak body that dies to everything, and the graveyard recast costs 2 life plus a sacrifice for the same fragile stats. Only a late-pick BG grinder; leave it in the sideboard if your deck is fine.
Wreckage Wickerfolk: Premium black common — first-pickable, take it every time. A 1/3 flyer for two with surveil 2 that feeds affinity (artifact), fuels graveyard BG, and provides Start-Your-Engines evasion; LoL calls it the best black common, 'did so much for every archetype.' 57.7% GIH at 89% play with +2.6 IWD; the C grade badly underrates it.
Wretched Doll: Filler/role-player — a 3/1 for two is fragile and off Scotty's 3-power-OR-3-toughness rule since it dies to everything, but the repeatable surveil feeds graveyard synergies. 55.1% GIH with a flat +0.6 IWD marks it as a replaceable body that only shines in BG self-mill; fine early curve filler, nothing to prioritize.
Adrenaline Jockey: Build-around role-player for exhaust decks (GB/RG), not a generic three-drop. The 4-damage punisher clause is real reach against control, and it grows off your exhaust triggers, but a vanilla-ish 3/3 with a negative -2.0 IWD tells you it underdelivers without the synergy. The 51.3% GIH is replacement-level; take it as a payoff, not a beater.
Boommobile: Premium rare, near-bomb. A 5/5 Crew-2 that ramps four on ETB then becomes repeatable X-damage removal — Flame Tongue-adjacent value stapled to a threat. 58.3% GIH, +5.4 IWD, ALSA 1.9 back the B+; the removal mode makes it far better than a vanilla vehicle. Slam it, especially in RG/RW/BR.
Burner Rocket: Filler combat trick on a body. Flash 3/1 that hands a creature +2/+0 and trample is a one-shot tempo/reach play, but the 3/1 crew-1 shell is fragile and 29.6% play rate / -1.8 IWD mark it fringe. A niche RW/aggro finisher, not a maindeck lock.
Burnout Bashtronaut: Excellent aggressive one-drop, take it early in red. Menace plus a pump into max-speed double strike makes it a mana sink and a real closer; the 64.2% OH WR and +6.0 IWD scream tempo. Best in BR/RW/UR aggro where it turns on speed and ends games — a top-tier commons-tier red card.
Chandra, Spark Hunter: Bomb, first-pick out of the pack. She protects herself by making 3/2 Vehicle tokens, filters cards, animates your vehicles with haste, and the ult ends games. 58.4% GIH, +5.9 IWD and a 1.3 ALSA (people slam her) confirm the mythic; take her over everything.
Clamorous Ironclad: The UR cycling backbone, a high pick in that lane. A 6/3 menace that cycles for R — as LoL says, 90% of the time you're cycling it to fuel Push the Limit, but cast it and six power tussles with green's fatties. 53.5% GIH is the floor; its real value is the flexibility, not the body.
Count on Luck: Trap rare — the numbers are damning. RRR upkeep card-advantage engine sounds good but the 49.8% GIH, -2.9 IWD and 24.2% play rate show it's too slow and does nothing the turn it lands. In a slow format you want board impact, not a durdle enchantment. Leave it; the D grade is right.
Crash and Burn: Solid removal, plays in nearly every red deck. Six damage kills all but the biggest green fatties and the modal vehicle-destroy covers the format's cars — clunky at {3}{R} and sorcery-speed-ish, but it gets the job done. 53.6% GIH is deflated by its cost; the near-universal 80% play rate is the real signal. Reliable mid-pick removal.
Daretti, Rocketeer Engineer: Role-player, best in an artifact deck. A */5 whose power keys off your biggest artifact and who recurs artifacts from the yard, so it needs UB/artifact density to shine — the poor 47.6% OH shows it flops when your board is light. 51.7% GIH and 44.6% play match the C; a build-around rare, not a slam.
Draconautics Engineer: Bomb-tier rare — first-pick it. The 1.6 ALSA, 61.7% GIH and enormous +8.6 IWD confirm the theory-grade A-: a 2/2 for two that either hastes your team and grows, or repeatedly makes 4/4 flyers, giving you a flood insurance value engine. One of the best red cards in the set; splash-worthy.
Dracosaur Auxiliary: Strong finisher, high pick. A 4/4 flyer-haste for six that pings 2 to any target each attack while saddled — immediate impact plus reach on a body that ends games. 54.7% GIH with +1.5 IWD is a touch soft for a bomb-ish rare because the saddle tax gates the burn, but the B- is right; great top-end for any red deck, best in RG/RW with cheap saddlers.
Dynamite Diver: Sideboard/role-player — a one-mana 1/1 Pilot that crews as power 3 and pings 1 on death, only worth running when your deck is genuinely vehicle-dense. 52.7% GIH, -0.5 IWD and a 35.7% play rate deflate the C+; it's a support piece for RW vehicles, otherwise a below-replacement two-drop-tier body you cut.
Endrider Catalyzer: A serviceable BR/aggro two-drop that doubles as a ramp/engine-starter — 3/1 that pings in for the Start Your Engines trigger, then taps for RR at max speed. The 3-power body dies easily and the 53.6% GIH is middling, but LoL confirms the double-mana upside is real. Role-player that's better in the dedicated speed deck than as a filler two-drop.
Endrider Spikespitter: Premium BR/aggro payoff despite the D+ theory grade. A 3/4 reach body is already fine defense, and at max speed it's a per-turn card-advantage "Howling Mine" for you only. 52.9% GIH undersells it because the number folds in decks that never hit max speed; in a real Start Your Engines shell it's a first-pickable engine. Trust the notes over the grade.
Fuel the Flames: Situational sweeper — 2 damage to each creature is a real board reset against go-wide or token decks, and cycling means it's never dead. But it kills your own board too, so it's a sideboard/flex card in most decks. 53.5% GIH is fine; 34.9% play rate reflects the matchup dependence.
Full Throttle: Trap — cut it. Six mana for extra combats in a slow, grindy format where you rarely have a wide untapped board to abuse it; 45.7% GIH, -5.5 IWD and F grade all agree. It's a win-more do-nothing when you're already ahead. Never maindeck.
Gastal Blockbuster: Sideboard-leaning filler. A 3/2 for three whose ETB only matters if the opponent has an artifact to blow up, and it costs you a creature/vehicle to do it — often a blank body in the maindeck. The 51.1% GIH and -1.8 IWD flag it as a matchup card; board it in against heavy artifact/vehicle decks.
Gastal Thrillroller: Excellent aggressive rare, high pick for RW/BR. A 4/2 trample-haste that swings the turn it lands, self-crews on ETB, and recurs itself from the yard — a relentless threat. 55.7% GIH with a 2.3 ALSA and B grade agree; one of the better red 3-drops for pushing early damage and Start Your Engines.
Gilded Ghoda: Below-replacement two-drop. A vanilla 2/2 that only makes a Treasure once you've saddled it — exactly the poorly-positioned 2-power body the format punishes (dies to 1/3s, no immediate impact). 52.8% GIH and negative IWD confirm the disappointment; playable ramp-fixer in RG/RW but never a priority pick.
Goblin Surveyor: Filler. A 3/2 trample two-drop that's below the format's curve (dies to 1/3s), redeemed only by a max-speed graveyard card-draw that requires you to already be winning. 51.6% GIH and -2.4 IWD confirm the C — a late-game gas replenisher for BR aggro, not a card you prioritize.
Greasewrench Goblin: Role-player, and a preview-hype card the pros walked back. A {R} 2/1 with a one-time loot+counter exhaust — fine early, but the small body blanks late and LoL admits 'you've been too high on this all format,' with Thunderhead Gunner miles better. The 57.5% GIH is inflated by early curve-out games; good, not great.
Hazoret, Godseeker: Powerful mythic but Max-Speed-gated — take it early, build to enable it. A 5/3 indestructible haste for two is absurd, but she can't attack or block until you're at Max Speed, so she needs the BR/aggro shell to turn on; 57.8% GIH / +5.5 IWD reflects real payoff once online. Discount slightly in slow, non-aggressive decks.
Howlsquad Heavy: Bomb — first pick, snap it. A 2/3 for three that makes a hasty attacker every combat and ramps hard at max speed; 61.8% GIH, elite +8.9 IWD, 1.8 ALSA and 88.5% play confirm it wins games well beyond a mere goblin-tribal payoff. Even outside a Goblin build the token engine plus mana are backbreaking. Best in BR/RG aggro.
Kickoff Celebrations: Niche build-around, mostly filler — a two-mana looter that later sacs for a team haste alpha strike, but the enchantment does nothing to the board on entry. 51.4% GIH and -1.0 IWD confirm the C-; it only earns a slot in UR Push-the-Limit / discard shells that want the loot trigger. Speculative pick, don't maindeck outside that lane.
Lightning Strike: Premium red removal you never cut — three damage to any target at instant speed kills most of the format and reaches faces. The 54.8% GIH and 3.4 ALSA slightly trail Thunderhead Gunner by retro, but LoL says take the first copy every time. High pick in any red deck; efficient interaction is scarce in this grind.
Magmakin Artillerist: Synergy role-player for UR/BR cycling-discard. A 1/4 that pings each opponent when you discard and can cycle itself for reach damage — chip damage plus a speed-turner in the discard deck. The 50.6% GIH and weak 47% OH WR show it's mediocre as a raw body; only strong once you have discard/cycling density. Mid pick in that lane.
Marauding Mako: The UR cycling/discard payoff — a one-mana 1/1 that snowballs with every discard and self-cycles if it's stranded. Strong 58.4% OH_WR and +4.1 IWD show it wants to hit the board turn one in the discard deck. Premium in UR, mediocre filler anywhere else; grade it up in-lane.
Outpace Oblivion: Premium red removal — high pick. Deal 5 to any creature/walker for {2}{R} kills nearly everything, and the sacrifice mode chips both opponents while your SYE deck races. 90.5% play and Ben's early pick confirm it; efficient enough for any red deck, best in BR/UR speed.
Pacesetter Paragon: Role-player in RW/exhaust. A 2/3 that presents a repeated 'threat of activation' — attack, and they either take a big double-strike hit or eat the counter permanently. The 51.5% GIH and -2.5 IWD say it's a grindy mana sink, not a bomb; the C+ is fair, a fine mid-pick body that scales late.
Pedal to the Metal: Filler combat trick / sideboard, a patience card. An XR first-strike pump can steal a game out of nowhere, but the -2.3 IWD and 7.8 ALSA show it's dead weight most games — you need a board and mana already ahead. Last-pick red, not maindeck unless you're the beatdown.
Prowcatcher Specialist: Filler two-drop. A 2/1 haste with a one-time exhaust pump to 4/3 is fine early aggression, but 2-power dies into the format's 1/3s and the exhaust costs a clunky {3}{R}. 52.3% GIH and -1.4 IWD mark it as replacement-level BR filler — a body when you're thin, not a card you reach for.
Push the Limit: Build-around bomb, hard trap otherwise. The Zenith Flare of DFT: in an assembled UR cycling deck with cycling vehicles + Thunderhead Gunner looting, it reanimates your yard and ends the game; out of it, it's unplayable. The D- grade and 23% play rate reflect the floor; the 54.4%/+5.0 IWD is the ceiling. Only take it when your UR mount/vehicle count (9+) supports it.
Reckless Velocitaur: Filler/trap outside a dedicated build. A 3/3 that only pays off when it saddles a Mount or crews a Vehicle on your main phase, demanding a critical mass of vehicles the slow format doesn't reward. The 49.3% GIH, -2.6 IWD and 30.7% play confirm the D+; leave it unless RW vehicles is wide open.
Road Rage: Efficient, scalable removal for vehicle decks — a strong pick in the right lane. For {R} it's always at least 2 damage and grows with your Mounts/Vehicles, making it clean removal in BR and RW; 56% GIH / +1.8 IWD backs the B grade. In a deck light on vehicles it's just a small burn spell — take with your artifact/vehicle count in mind.
Skycrash: Maindeckable role-player, take it as a red support card. Artifact removal that cycles for {R} when dead — the format's real threats (River Monument, Aether Syphon, Vehicles) make it live in the main, and cheap cycling fuels UR Push the Limit. 54.5% GIH with +1.1 IWD earns the B-; flexible, never a wasted slot.
Spire Mechcycle: Overgraded on paper — the B grade is a trap the live data busts: 49.9% GIH and -2.6 IWD. A hasty 5/4 vehicle that grows via exhaust, but it needs a board of other Mounts/Vehicles to pop off and does little on its own in this slow format. Only a real card in a dedicated RW/vehicle deck; otherwise a mediocre five-drop.
Thunderhead Gunner: The top red common and a genuine overperformer — take it ahead of even Lightning Strike. A 4/5 reach for five blocks everything, and the loot-each-turn ability fuels UR cycling/discard while smoothing draws. The 56.1% GIH and LoL's 'Imperial Oath' clunky-overperformer nod confirm it plays far above its C grade; a slam in any red deck.
Tyrox, Saurid Tyrant: Aggressive role-player. A 4/1 for two hits hard early and pilots/saddles well but dies to everything and is a poor blocker in this slow format — exactly the fragile two-drop archetype the doctrine warns about. 53.3% GIH leans on aggro starts; playable in BR/RW aggro, filler elsewhere.
Afterburner Expert: Near-bomb rare and a top pick. A 4/2 that grows +2/+2 via exhaust AND recurs itself from the graveyard every time you exhaust — a recursive, hard-to-kill threat that dodges removal. Excellent 59.1% GIH, 1.7 ALSA, 91% play rate. Slam it in any green deck, especially BG/RG exhaust.
Agonasaur Rex: Bomb — first-pick it. An 8/8 trample for 5 that, when you can't afford it, cycles for {2}{G} to draw AND slap two counters plus trample/indestructible on a creature or vehicle — it is never a dead card. 64.3% GIH, +10 IWD, 1.5 ALSA; the best green common-slot payoff, splashable anywhere green.
Alacrian Jaguar: Filler, below its stats suggest. A 4/4 vigilance for five that needs to be saddled to become a 6/6 attacker — a lot of setup for a slow ground body in a slow format. The 50.7% GIH and -3.1 IWD earn the D+; only a saddle-heavy GW deck wants it, otherwise it's a late-pick 23rd card.
Autarch Mammoth: Premium green uncommon, high pick in any green deck. A 5/5 for six that makes a 3/3 on ETB and another every attack once saddled — it snowballs bodies and outgrinds board stalls. 58.3% GIH, 2.6 ALSA, and 92.8% play rate back the B grade; slam it, best in GB/RG where saddle enablers exist.
Beastrider Vanguard: Solid green role-player, not a 2/2 to dismiss. The {4}{G} dig-for-a-permanent mana sink gives this a relevant late game the format rewards, so it curves early and doesnt rot in the mid-game. The ~0 IWD says it wins by being cast on-curve, not by being drawn — a dependable BG/green-midrange filler, and its C grade is about right.
Bestow Greatness: Role-player combat trick. +4/+4 and trample is a blowout with deathtouchers and enables profitable attacks/blocks vs. big green, but tricks are risky in a grindy format and this is card disadvantage. 55.7% GIH with a flat IWD marks it a green sideboard-to-main flex; good in the mirror, not a first pick.
Broken Wings: Sideboard-leaning role-player. Instant-speed destruction of artifacts, enchantments, or flyers is narrow — it whiffs on ground creatures — but green needs cheap interaction and this handles vehicles and evasion. 55.0% GIH tops the C-, though the negative IWD flags it as situational; a fine 22nd-24th card, better postboard.
Defend the Rider: Premium modal trick — 'very very good' per LoL, better than its flat +0.2 IWD suggests. A {G} instant that either blanks removal/wins combat with hexproof-indestructible or makes a crewing Pilot is pure patience-card upside; the low IWD reflects that it needs the right board, not that it's weak. A high pick in any green deck.
District Mascot: Excellent one-drop, high pick — take it. A {G} 1/1 that grows via saddle attacks and doubles as repeatable artifact removal, curving early and scaling late. 63.9% OH WR shows it's fine in your opener; the gap down to 54.3% GD WR means it's best cast on turn one, not drawn late. C+ undersells a flexible aggressive Mount for any green deck.
Dredger's Insight: Role-player enabler for graveyard decks — self-mills four and digs for a card on entry, then trickles life as your yard is used. 57.3% GIH but a modest +1.1 IWD flags it as synergy glue, not a standalone card; the C- is fair for random decks. Prioritize in BG graveyard-value, where it smooths the deck and feeds reanimation.
Earthrumbler: A wire-to-wire bomb-uncommon — a 7/6 vigilance-trample vehicle that's trivially crewed at 3, or self-animates by exiling from your graveyard so it's never a dead card. This is the beatdown-and-block engine BG/RG stompy wants. The 55.6% GIH understates it (green fatties get built to enable), but the 3.1 ALSA and 89.8% play rate show everyone takes it early. High pick.
Elvish Refueler: Solid glue and the exhaust "lord" for GU/GB exhaust decks. A 2/3 that lets you re-fire one exhaust ability per turn multiplies your best buttons (Hazard, Earthrumbler); 55.4% GIH and 90% play rate beat the C grade. Even the self-pump keeps it relevant off-synergy. Good early pick in green.
Fang Guardian: Reliable green playable with real flexibility. Flash 4/2 that pumps another creature or Vehicle +2/+2 doubles as a combat ambush and a crew/attack enabler. 56.6% GIH and 89% play rate outrun the C+ grade; a clean two-for-one blowout in any green midrange deck.
Fang-Druid Summoner: Solid green value creature. A {3}{G} 2/4 reach that tutors a no-abilities creature from library OR graveyard — card advantage plus a body that blocks fliers and ground. 57.8% GIH; the C grade underrates it. Best in green beatdown/BG where it fetches your fatties and rebuys the yard.
Greenbelt Guardian: Excellent — a premium green two-drop. It has 3 toughness (beating Scotty's rule), the trample-grant enables your fatties through chumps, and exhaust turns it into a 5/5 late. 58.2% GIH, +2.5 IWD and a 2.6 ALSA (drafters value it) beat the B-; a high pick in any green deck.
Hazard of the Dunes: Format-defining green common, take it highly. A 4/4 trample-reach for four sets the rules of engagement — blocks everything relevant and its exhaust makes it a 7/7 threat later. The 56.9% GIH is honest here (not ramp-inflated), and near-universal play backs it; every green deck wants multiples.
Jibbirik Omnivore: Fine aggressive common — a 3/2 for two clears Scotty's "3 power" bar, so it's a real two-drop unlike the vanilla 2/2s. 57.0% OH WR shows it does its job as an early attacker before the format slows down, but the -1.1 IWD says it fades late. Solid green filler; play it, don't prioritize it.
Loxodon Surveyor: Filler — a disappointing vanilla 3/3 for three whose only text is a max-speed graveyard draw that green rarely turns on. Scotty's bar barely cleared and it doesn't advance the board. 53.9% GIH and -1.8 IWD confirm the C; a body to round out a green curve, nothing more.
Lumbering Worldwagon: First-pick-caliber ramp payoff — take it over almost anything. A {2}{G} vehicle that fetches a basic every attack (and on ETB), fixing, ramping, and growing into a huge crew-4 threat. The absurd 65.4% GIH, +11.6 IWD and 1.5 ALSA blow past the B; it's the engine that makes green late-game decks hum.
March of the World Ooze: Bomb — a game-ending green mythic. Turning your whole team into 6/6 Oozes ends the game fast and the Elephant clause taxes opponents' interaction; 62.7% GIH and a massive +9.0 IWD confirm it, though that number is inflated by the ramp/green decks best able to cast {3}{G}{G}{G}. Slam it in any green deck.
Migrating Ketradon: Premium green common — take it highly. A 6/6 reach for six that gains 4 life and, crucially, cycles {2} when you don't want the fatty, so it's never dead in the grindy format. 57.5% GIH at 90% play with the reach wall stopping green's own flyers; note GIH slightly inflates green fatties, but the cycling flexibility makes this a genuine C+-beating staple.
Molt Tender: Excellent common fixer and a high pick for green decks — a one-drop that fixes any color and self-mills to feed the graveyard. 57.4% GIH with a strong 61.6% OH shows it's best deployed turn one (fixing + enabling); LoL loves it for BG. The 4.0 ALSA means it goes early — grab it to enable splashes and graveyard synergies.
Ooze Patrol: A payoff for BG/graveyard decks that's below replacement elsewhere. In a fresh game it's a 2/2-ish for four; with a stocked yard it's a huge body that also self-mills for your reanimation. The 54.6% GIH beats the D+ grade only when the deck supports it — the flat +0.1 IWD flags its variance. Take it as a synergy piece, not a curve-filler.
Oviya, Automech Artisan: Build-around rare, provisional playable. A 1/2 that grants attackers trample and cheats a creature/Vehicle out per turn (doubling artifacts with counters) is powerful in a dedicated fatty/vehicle deck but fragile and slow. 53.3% GIH with near-flat IWD undercuts the ceiling implied by the text; the D+ grade is closer to right than the hype. Take it as a synergy piece, not a bomb.
Plow Through: Premium green removal at one mana — modal fight OR straight Vehicle destruction covers the format's whole threat range. Green's answer to big green mirrors. 55.4% GIH; the number is deflated by needing a creature to fight, but the flexibility earns the B grade. Early pick in any G deck.
Point the Way: Trap — don't play it. A speed-gated ramp enchantment that does nothing the turn it lands and only ramps meaningfully once you're at high speed, which ramp decks aren't; 43.6% GIH, -6.3 IWD, 8.7% play and F grade are unanimous. Fixing this bad isn't worth a card. Cut.
Pothole Mole: Solid playable, quietly above rate. A 2/3 for three (good toughness) that mills three and rebuys a land, smoothing your draws and enabling graveyard payoffs in BG. The 56.7% GIH and 82% play rate outrun its C+; a reliable early-mid pick that curves and feeds the graveyard deck.
Regal Imperiosaur: Excellent green rare, first-pickable. A 5/4 for three is enormous stats even ignoring the (usually irrelevant) Dino anthem — it dominates the board on curve in a format where 4-toughness matters. 57.6% GIH, 2.1 ALSA, and 91% play rate all confirm the beater; splashable into any G deck.
Rise from the Wreck: Niche value card, not maindeck default. Returning up to four graveyard cards is powerful in a grindy BG shell, but the split WR (49.8% OH / 56.5% GD) and D+ grade show it's dead early and only shines late with a stocked yard. Playable as a one-of in BG value; leave it otherwise.
Run Over: Premium green removal, take it early. Fight-without-the-fight: your creature deals its power with no damage back, costing as little as {G} off a mount/vehicle — perfect for green's oversized bodies. The 93.8% play rate, 3.1 ALSA and 57.3% GIH crush the C+ grade; one of the best green commons in the set.
Silken Strength: Filler/sideboard combat trick. Flash +1/+2 and reach with an untap is mainly a blowout against fight removal like Flood the Engine, but LoL notes green has better maindeck options and Ben isn't keen on it. The 54.6% GIH looks fine yet the 24% play and 7.5 ALSA say it's a niche, situational include.
Stampeding Scurryfoot: Green's best-in-class common one-drop — pick it highly. A 1/1 for {G} looks weak but the exhaust makes a 3/3 Elephant plus a counter, giving a mono-green mana sink that's 'explosively synergistic with exhaust payoffs'; 58.6% GIH and a 93% play rate prove it. Core green/BG/GU card, great with exhaust matters-payoffs.
Terrian, World Tyrant: Solid green top-end, take it — but it's a raw beater, not a bomb. A 9/7 for five drops as the biggest body on the board and simply stomps in green-on-green stalls; 56.7% GIH and 86% play back the C+. GIH overrates green fatties conditioned on the ramp deck, so weight it toward BG/RG/green-ramp shells that can protect and deploy it.
Thunderous Velocipede: First-pick bomb — a 1GG 5/5 trample that also anthems every future creature and vehicle with +1/+1 counters (three if MV 5+). A turn-three 5/5 in a slow format is absurd, and the counters snowball the whole board. 57.4% GIH is deflated by its 1.4 ALSA and 91% play (everyone forces it in); trust the B+ and slam it.
Veloheart Bike: A flexible role-player — a 4/2 crew-2 vehicle that gains 2 life on ETB and, crucially, taps for any color of mana, doubling as fixing for greedy/multicolor decks. The 55.6% GIH is solid and the mana ability quietly enables splashes. Not exciting on rate, but the fixing-plus-body package earns a maindeck slot in most green or 3-color decks.
Venomsac Lagac: Solid green common. A 2/1 deathtouch for two already trades up and picks off anything, and saddled it becomes a 2/4 wall — deathtouch plus 4 toughness is exactly what the format rewards. 55.9% GIH and 92% play rate outrun the C grade; a dependable early pick that's good even without Mounts.
Webstrike Elite: Flexible green rare that's always live — a 3/3 reach body when you need pressure, or scalable X-cost cycling that draws AND blows up an artifact/enchantment. Never a dead card. 57.5% GIH, 2.2 ALSA, 91% play rate. Take it high; the C+ grade underrates the mode-switching value.
Aatchik, Emerald Radian: Bomb and the BG signpost — first-pick it in the best deck. ETB floods the board with Insects off your graveyard, then every Insect death grows it and drains, giving a self-fueling aristocrats engine. 58.3% GIH understates it (61.3% drawn); take it, then draft BG graveyard/exhaust around it.
Apocalypse Runner: Good in the right deck, but a known trap-over-removal. A 6/5 vehicle at crew 3 that makes a small creature unblockable with lifelink — a real BR finisher, but the retro correction is clear: don't take it over removal. The 53.6% GIH and C fit; a solid mid-pick, not a first pick.
Boom Scholar: The RG signpost and exhaust engine, but a modest pick. A 3/3 that makes every exhaust ability cost 2 less turns Hazard/Earthrumbler buttons into repeatable value, plus its own trample-alpha finisher. The flat 53.6% GIH and C+ grade show it's build-around, not a bomb — take it when committed to RG/green exhaust.
Boosted Sloop: Solid UR uncommon. A 3/3 menace with crew 1 that loots on every attack fuels cycling/discard-matters while evading — and crew 1 means almost anything can activate it. +2.5 IWD and B- grade back it up; the 54.0% GIH is dragged by non-synergy decks. Good pick in UR, a fine body anywhere blue-red.
Brightglass Gearhulk: Bomb-tier gold uncommon-feel mythic for GW artifacts. A 4/4 first strike trample for four is already ahead of the curve, and the ETB tutors two cheap artifacts/creatures/enchantments to fuel affinity and Starting Column decks. 60.5% GIH, +6.7 IWD, 60% OH all agree it's well above its B; slam in any GW deck.
Broadside Barrage: Premium multicolor removal — take it highly in UR. 5 damage kills nearly the whole format at instant speed, and the loot feeds Push the Limit/discard-matters exactly where you want it. 58.2% GIH, +5.4 IWD and a strong 59.9% drawn beat the B; a top reason to be in UR cycling and a signpost of the archetype.
Broodheart Engine: Grindy BG value piece, a bit better than its C- grade. Upkeep surveil filters and the reanimation sac returns a fat creature or Vehicle, feeding the S-tier BG graveyard plan; 56.9% GIH / +1.7 IWD says it's a solid but slow role-player, not a bomb. Prioritize when you're the BG grind deck, filler otherwise.
Captain Howler, Sea Scourge: Bomb-tier UR payoff — first-pickable if you're in the lane. A 5/4 ward body that turns every discard into a huge pump-and-draw, exactly the UR cycling/discard engine; 58.8% GIH, +8.3 IWD and 2.9 ALSA confirm the B and then some. Wants Clamorous Ironclad-style cyclers to pop off; still a fine standalone threat.
Caradora, Heart of Alacria: Strong signpost rare and a high pick — a 4/2 for four that tutors any Mount or Vehicle to hand and adds an extra +1/+1 counter to every counter effect, a real payoff for a counters/vehicles build. 57.8% GIH and B+ align; the fragile 4/2 body wants support, so it's best in its WG lane where the tutor and counter engine both fire.
Cloudspire Coordinator: The RW vehicles/pilot signpost and a strong build-around uncommon — scry 2 on ETB, then a token engine that snowballs off every Mount/Vehicle you land. LoL calls it oppressive in RW and GW. But the 54.4% GIH and low 47.7% play rate reflect that RW is hard to pilot; premium when the lane is open, replacement-level when your board is thin.
Cloudspire Skycycle: Role-player for RW vehicles. A 2/3 flier Crew-1 that distributes two counters on ETB is fine two-for-one board development, but the sub-50% OH WR and 48% play rate show it needs the crew-heavy shell to matter. The B- grade overshoots the 50.3% live WR; a decent mid pick in RW, cuttable elsewhere.
Coalstoke Gearhulk: Bomb-tier BR mythic. A 5/4 menace-deathtouch is already hard to block, and the ETB reanimates a value creature with haste for a turn — reach, tempo, and a graveyard payoff in one. 55.4% GIH is muted by the double-double cost; +3.5 IWD and B+ grade say slam it in any BR shell.
Debris Beetle: Bomb-adjacent — take it very high. A {2}{B}{G} 6/6 trample that ETBs a 6-point life swing (3 drain + 3 gain), immediately stabilizing and threatening lethal; crew 2 is trivial. 61.4% GIH and +7.9 IWD earn better than its B+. Premium BG top-end, splashable in any deck touching both colors.
Dune Drifter: Strong pick in WB/graveyard. An X-cost 3/3 vehicle that reanimates a creature or artifact from your yard for value, scaling with the game — flexible and always relevant. The 54.1% GIH plus a big gap between OH (51.1%) and drawn (56.0%) mark it as a value card that gets better later; the B grade is right.
Embalmed Ascendant: Strong WB signpost, high pick. Three mana for effectively 3/3 of stats (1/2 plus a 2/2 Zombie) with a Blood Artist drain at max speed — exactly the WB aristocrats payoff. 59.2% GIH and +5.6 IWD beat the B grade; the ETB token gives it a real floor even before speed comes online.
Explosive Getaway: High pick — a wheel-able sweeper the field disrespected. It blinks your own creature (or resets an artifact) then deals 4 to all creatures, so you can wrath the board one-sided. LoL: "massively underrated," came late because white was ignored. +4.3 IWD and A- grade are real; take it early and go big white / Push the Limit.
Far Fortune, End Boss: Bomb and the BR signpost. A 4/5 for four is a great body on its own; the attack trigger pings for reach and, at max speed, adds +1 to ALL your damage — a runaway engine that turns burn and combat into overkill. 59.4% GIH and +7.1 IWD confirm it's a top-tier BR build-around; first-pick quality.
Fearless Swashbuckler: Strong build-around rare, near-first-pickable in the right lane. A {1}{U}{R} 3/3 haste that gives vehicles haste and draws three when a Pirate and Vehicle both attack — an explosive card-advantage engine in UR vehicles/Pirates. 55.4% GIH and +4.4 IWD support the B, though it needs the pieces to fully break open.
Gastal Thrillseeker: Strong BR two-drop — take it as a signpost. A 2/3 for {B}{R} that pings, gains life to start your engines, then becomes a deathtouch-haste attacker at Max Speed is exactly what BR wants; 59.8% GIH with a big +6.0 IWD and 61% OH_WR confirm the aggressive body pulls its weight early and late.
Guidelight Pathmaker: Strong role-player, high pick in artifact decks. A 6/5 vigilance vehicle for six that tutors an artifact — cheating a 2-or-less onto the battlefield or grabbing a bomb — real card advantage plus a hard-to-attack-through body. 56.8% GIH with +5.7 IWD beats the C grade; best in WU/UB artifact shells but the raw stats play anywhere. Needs crew.
Haunt the Network: Premium build-around and the reason to draft UB affinity — makes two flying Thopters and drains X equal to your artifacts, a swingy tempo-and-life haymaker. 59.7% GIH with a massive +7.7 IWD and 62.9% GD WR crush the C+; that number IS the artifact deck (LoL's 'Zenith Flare', combos with Pactdoll Terror). Prioritize highly if you're in UB.
Haunted Hellride: The UB signpost — a 3/3 crew-1 vehicle that hands a creature deathtouch and untaps it every attack, so it trades up and ambushes while attacking. Good engine for the grindy UB control plan. The 53.1% GIH and 48.7% play rate are modest because it needs board presence to shine; a solid role-player in the archetype, filler outside it.
Ketramose, the New Dawn: Trap in Limited despite the mythic aura. It can't attack or block until seven cards are in exile — a condition DFT decks rarely reach — so it's often a do-nothing 4/4 that just draws you a card or two. 46.9% GIH, 9% play rate and null OH/GD WR confirm it's near-unplayable; provisional read, but leave it in the binder.
Kolodin, Triumph Caster: Build-around WR two-drop, not a slam. Free haste plus auto-saddle/auto-crew is a bomb enabler ONLY with a critical mass of Mounts and Vehicles — outside that shell it's a vanilla 2/3. B+ grade reflects the ceiling; the flat 51.2% GIH shows how often the deck isn't there. RW payoff card.
Lagorin, Soul of Alacria: Good WG/RW Mount uncommon, solid pick. A {G}{W} 1/1 flyer with cheap saddle-1 that dumps two counters onto Mounts/Vehicles per attack — evasive and a fast counter engine. 55.3% GIH, 58.4% OH; take it in counters/Mount aggro, but it's fragile and needs a saddle target to matter.
Loot, the Pathfinder: Bomb — arguably a first-pick-worthy mythic if you can cast it. A 2/4 double-strike/vigilance/haste body that fixes, draws three, or Bolts anything across three exhaust modes. The 63.9% GIH and monster +12.0 IWD blow past the cautious B-; slam it and commit to Temur/URG.
Mendicant Core, Guidelight: Powerful WU/artifact rare, high pick in that lane. A 2-drop that grows with your artifact count and copies your artifact spells at max speed — a snowballing engine in affinity shells. 56.3% GIH and +5.0 IWD support the B grade; needs an artifact-dense deck, so provisional in a light-artifact build.
Mimeoplasm, Revered One: Build-around mythic — powerful ceiling, awkward floor. It's a graveyard-fueled scaling body that copies exiled creatures, ideal for BG/Sultai value, but the ugly 46.3% OH vs 54.0% GD split shows it's terrible early and needs a full yard. 51.0% GIH tempers the B grade; a strong midlate payoff, not a turn-one keep.
Oildeep Gearhulk: Bomb for UB. A 4/4 lifelink ward-1 for four is hard to kill and swings races, and the ETB is a Thoughtseize-plus-loot that strips their best card. The +8.4 IWD (one of the highest here) and 58.6% GIH exceed the B+; a premier UB artifact/control payoff, take it very early.
Pyrewood Gearhulk: Bomb — first-pick it. A {2}{RRGG} 7/7 vigilance/menace that anthems your team +2/+2 with keywords and stops damage prevention, ending games the turn it lands. 60.8% GIH, +8.4 IWD and 2.2 ALSA confirm the A; the payoff that makes RG stompy worth drafting, even at a demanding double-double cost.
Rangers' Aetherhive: Solid GU exhaust payoff — trust the B- grade. A crew-1 3/5 vigilance is a sturdy blocker on its own, and every exhaust activation spits a Thopter, snowballing the go-wide exhaust plan; 54.9% GIH / +0.2 IWD is muted because it needs exhaust density. Prioritize in GU; a fine defensive body anywhere it fits.
Redshift, Rocketeer Chief: Role-player rare, take it in RG. A 2/3 vigilance that ramps ability-only mana equal to its power and has a splashy 10-mana exhaust dump; the mana engine feeds RG's big exhaust payloads. 54.3% GIH and +0.4 IWD are modest — the OH-over-GD gap (56.4 vs 52.7) says play it early as a ramp piece, not draw it as a bomb. C+ is fair.
Riptide Gearhulk: Format-defining bomb — a double-striking, prowess-boosted 2/5 that time-walks each opponent's best permanent to third-from-top on entry, a two-for-one that also races. 62.8% GIH and a monstrous +14.7 IWD prove it wins games by itself; the demanding WWUU cost is the only cost. First-pick it and commit to WU. Trust the number over the B+.
Rocketeer Boostbuggy: The RG signpost and a genuinely good vehicle — crew 1, makes a Treasure every attack (ramp and fixing), and exhausts to become a growing creature on its own. The 56.3% GIH with a strong 59.9% OH_WR confirms it plays great early. LoL's 'a lot of goodies' is right; a high pick in RG/exhaust and a fine inclusion in any red-green deck.
Sab-Sunen, Luxa Embodied: Format-defining bomb, first pick over almost anything. A 6/6 reach/trample/indestructible that draws two every other turn and is nearly unkillable — the counter clause is a non-issue. 67.9% GIH, +15.4 IWD, ALSA 1.3, A+: as good as the numbers get. If you see it, take it and play GU.
Samut, the Driving Force: Powerful WRG rare and a strong first pick if you're in Naya. First strike/vigilance/haste 4/5 that anthems your team and discounts spells as speed climbs — a snowballing engine that turns on fast. 56.1% GIH, +3.8 IWD; the three-color cost is the only real cost. Grade B+ is right.
Sita Varma, Masked Racer: Strong GU exhaust payoff — high pick. A cheap {G}{U} 2/3 that later dumps X counters on itself and can mass-buff your whole team to its power for a one-shot alpha finish; 60.2% GIH and +6.8 IWD confirm the ceiling. Best in GU/green exhaust ramp where you have mana and bodies to overrun with.
Skyserpent Seeker: Premium two-drop for GU. A 1/1 flyer with deathtouch trades up all day and blocks anything, then exhaust ramps two lands and grows it — evasion plus fixing plus mana. The 59.2% GIH and +4.4 IWD crush its B-; an early pick in any green-blue deck and fine glue elsewhere.
Thundering Broodwagon: Premium BG uncommon, a top pick and the S-tier signpost. Six mana for a 6/5 menace-reach that Murders a nonland permanent (MV 4 or less) on crew, and cycles when you can't crew — no downside. 61.1% GIH, +5.9 IWD, and universal play make it a slam; removal stapled to a huge evasive body.
Veteran Beastrider: Take it highly — one of the format's best uncommons on rate. A 3/4 for three already blocks everything relevant (4-toughness magic number), the end-step untap enables vigilant attacks/blocks, and the anthem closes games. 59.7% GIH, +4.6 IWD, splashable — LoL loved it in big white/WG. Trust the numbers over the B grade.
Voyage Home: Solid card-advantage payoff for artifact decks. Draw three, gain three — with affinity it's routinely a {3}- or {4}-mana Concentrate in UB/WU/UR, exactly the refuel a grindy control deck wants. 56.1% GIH and a strong +7.9pp OH→GD gap (a drawn/late card) match the B-; a fine mid-pick when your artifact count is high.
Winter, Cursed Rider: Strong two-drop, best in UB artifacts. A {U}{B} 3/2 that wards your whole artifact board and, with graveyard artifacts to exile, fires a scalable board-shrinking -X/-X — removal stapled to an aggressive body. 55.6% GIH and +3.8 IWD edge past the B-; a flexible early play that rewards the UB affinity shell it signposts.
Zahur, Glory's Past: Strong WB aristocrats signpost — better than the modest play rate suggests. A 3/2 for two with a repeatable sac-to-surveil and a Max-Speed Zombie engine rewards the sacrifice deck; 57% GIH and +4.6 IWD confirm the B grade. High pick if WB is open; needs the sac/aristocrats shell to shine, so pass it out of that lane.
Aetherjacket: Sideboard/filler. A 3-mana 2/1 flyer-vigilance that sacs to kill an artifact — narrow, and the 2/1 body dies to everything in a format where 3-toughness is the entry fee. 50.9% GIH, negative IWD and 35% play confirm the D+; only maindeck it when artifacts are a real problem, otherwise it's a marginal colorless flyer.
The Aetherspark: Colorless mythic bomb, a P1P1 in any deck — a 1.0 ALSA and 99.4% play rate mean it's taken every single time. A four-mana planeswalker-equipment that snowballs loyalty off combat damage, then draws two or ramps ten. 60.9% GIH and +9.0 IWD confirm it slots into and wins for any archetype. Take it over almost anything.
Camera Launcher: Colorless filler that finds a home in exhaust/artifact decks (GU thopters, UB artifacts). A 2/2 for three is below the format's curve, but the exhaust makes a flying Thopter and grows itself, adding an evasive body and artifact count. The 53.5% GIH and 42.9% play rate mark it as a role-player — playable glue, never a priority pick.
Guidelight Matrix: Underrated glue for UB artifact and Big White. A 2-mana artifact that replaces itself and taps to crew/saddle for free — it triggers Pactdoll Terror, counts for Haunt the Network, and crews Marshals' Pathcruiser. 53.0% GIH with a low 20% play rate means it shines only in the built decks; a smart late-pick synergy enabler, not a maindeck default.
Lifecraft Engine: Middling colorless build-around — a 4/4 crew-3 that lords over your Vehicles by naming a type. Needs a Vehicle-dense board to matter, and crew 3 is stiff. 51.6% GIH and flat IWD say it's a role-player in dedicated vehicle decks (WU/RW), not the generic playable the colorless slot suggests.
Marketback Walker: Flexible colorless role-player, near-universal include (97% play). An {X}{X} scaling body that draws cards equal to its counters when it dies, so it's never a blank — fills your curve at any point and replaces itself. 56.6% GIH, +3.0 IWD; a fine pick in any deck, better with the {4} counter sink in grindy shells.
Marshals' Pathcruiser: Strong colorless playable, great in the 4c/fixing shell. A 6/5 for three (crew 5 is steep) that fetches a basic to smooth mana, and the five-color exhaust makes it a self-crewing 8/7. The 58.8% GIH and +4.5 IWD beat its C grade; the ramp-and-fix package makes this a solid pick for any deck.
Monument to Endurance: Underrated colorless build-around, best in UR/UB cycling. Every discard drains 3, ramps, or draws — 'the best cycling payoff' that closes games in the discard deck. The D grade and 51.5% GIH are dragged down by non-cycling decks playing it; in the right shell it's a bomb, out of it a nonbo.
Pit Automaton: Niche uncommon, not the format staple one guide claimed. A 0/4 defender that ramps colorless for abilities and copies an exhaust trigger — genuinely strong only in dedicated GU/BG exhaust decks (Ethan's read), a durdle elsewhere. 54.0% GIH and D+ grade favor the tepid take. Speculative pick unless your exhaust density is high.
Racers' Scoreboard: Trap / sideboard. A {4} do-nothing that loots two on ETB, then only pays off at max speed — the exact speed most non-aggro decks never reach. 48% GIH, -1.6 IWD and a 7.2% play rate all scream unplayable; the D- is earned. Leave it in the pool.
Radiant Lotus: Trap/sideboard in Limited. A six-mana rock that only makes mana by sacrificing your own artifacts — a build-around ritual with no board impact and no reliable payoff in draft. Null WR on 0.3% play plus the F grade make this an easy pass; provisional read, but everything points to unplayable.
Rover Blades: Below-replacement trap despite double strike — the D+ grade and 49.8% GIH / -2.4 IWD agree. It's a clunky crew-2 2/2 or a {4} equip that's a two-for-one waiting to happen, far too slow for this grindy format. Sideboard/last-pick material; don't be seduced by double strike.
Scrap Compactor: Clunky but necessary removal — take it as a colorless answer to what your colors can't kill. Overcosted at {6} for the destroy mode, but LoL notes it kills Migrating Ketradon and green fatties nothing else touches, and it's demoralizing when you're ahead. 53.8% GIH with 57% play; the D grade undersells its role as insurance in removal-light decks.
Skybox Ferry: Filler/sideboard — a 5-mana 4/4 flyer with cheap Crew 2, and the {2} cycling keeps it from ever being dead, which is its only real virtue. 50.3% GIH, -0.1 IWD and 18% play rate match the D+; a flat evasive body that's below replacement in a slow format. Play it as a last-slot cycler in a flyers-light deck, cut it otherwise.
Starting Column: The set's best connective tissue — the 'Golden Egg' that fixes mana (any color), turns on Start Your Engines, and cashes into card selection at max speed. Its low D+ grade and 54.1% GIH undersell it because it's a support piece, not a threat; LoL calls it juicy in Mardu/Esper piles. A high pick specifically for greedy multicolor and speed decks.
Ticket Tortoise: Filler/fixing role-player. A 3/1 defender that sometimes makes a Treasure when behind on lands — an artifact for affinity plus a splash-enabler and a wall against aggro. 53.3% GIH but low IWD and 34% play rate mark it as a specific-deck card (artifact/splash builds). Late pick when you need fixing or artifact count.
Walking Sarcophagus: Below-replacement filler. A colorless 2/1 that becomes a 3/3 only at max speed is a weak two-drop by Scotty's rule (no 3 power/toughness on curve), and the payoff lags the format's slow speed. 52.9% GIH is deck-fixing charity; 42.6% play rate and -0.7 IWD confirm you can do better.
Wreck Remover: Filler — near the bottom of playables. A {4} 3/4 with minor graveyard hate and 1 life on ETB/attack, plus cycling so it's never dead. 52.5% GIH, D+ grade, 25% play: replacement-level body you run when short. Cycle it or sideboard the exile against BG graveyard decks.
Amonkhet Raceway: Filler land for aggressive decks. A colorless-only tapland that grants haste at max speed — narrow, and the colorless mana strains two-color manabases. The 52.1% GIH and -2.3 IWD (it's a mana source, not a spell) show it's marginal; only a mono-leaning or BR aggro deck should run it over a basic.
Avishkar Raceway: Fringe utility land / sideboard. A colorless-only tap land whose max-speed loot is too slow and mana-hungry to matter — 7.7 ALSA and D- grade say most decks can't afford the colorless slot. Only for heavy-artifact or fixing-starved builds; a deck-thinning liability otherwise.
Bleachbone Verge: Playable dual land — solid fixing for WB and any black splash. The Plains/Swamp condition is trivial to meet in-color, so it's an untapped source most games. 54.7% GIH and +1.2 IWD are just the fixing-helps-consistency premium; take it over marginal spells when your mana needs it, not as a spell slot.
