Bloodfell Caves: Playable fixing for two-color BR/Mardu decks. The tapland lifegain matters little in this slow format but the mana fixing is real, especially for splashing. 54% GIH is deck-quality noise; the 51.8% play rate is the honest read — take it as a fixer, never over a spell.
Blossoming Sands: Solid playable fixing for GW. A tapland that gains a life and taps for green or white — the standard dual that smooths two-color and splash manabases in a grindy format where the tempo loss barely matters. 54.8% GIH and the C+ align; a fine early-to-mid pick when you're settled into a green-white pairing.
Country Roads: Marginal fixing land — playable only in dedicated vehicle/RW decks. It enters tapped without a Mount/Vehicle and taps for white, with a late sac-for-Pilot mode; 53.5% GIH / -2.2 IWD shows the tempo cost usually isn't worth it. Late pick that helps a Push-the-Limit/vehicles manabase, cuttable elsewhere.
Dismal Backwater: Playable fixing, take it when you're UB or splashing. Taplands are fine in this slow format — the tempo hit rarely matters and the 1 life is real; 55.4% GIH and +1.8 IWD reflect the deck-smoothing, not card power. Standard dual-land pick; grab it to enable a splash, not over playables.
Foul Roads: Role-player fixing land — enters untapped only with a Mount/Vehicle, taps for black, and sacs late for a Pilot token to crew/saddle. 54.9% GIH and -0.8 IWD put it below the C+ hype; it's a flex land for black-based vehicle decks that occasionally wants the token. Fine 40th card in RW/WB vehicles, not a priority pick.
Jungle Hollow: A BG dual land — enters tapped, gains a life, taps for B or G. Fixing is real value in a format that rewards splashing removal, and the 55.4% GIH reflects the decks that run it rather than the card's power. Take it appropriately for any black-green or splash deck; the tapland cost is minor in this slow format.
Muraganda Raceway: Trap — an F-graded colorless land that only taps for {C}. It gives nothing until max speed and then just doubles into colorless, so it neither fixes nor ramps a two-color deck usefully. The -2.0 IWD and 51.1% WR (buoyed by mono-ish decks) confirm it: don't run it unless you're colorless-heavy.
Night Market: Premium fixing — take it early and run every copy. A cycling dual land that fixes any color and is never a dead draw thanks to cycling; LoL calls it a top-10 common and the set's best fixer. 95% play rate. Enables greedy splashes and the 4c good-stuff piles. The C+ grade badly underrates it.
Reef Roads: Playable utility land for blue Mount/Vehicle decks. Comes in untapped if you have a Mount/Vehicle, taps for {U}, and late-game sacs into a Pilot that crews/saddles for +2 power — real fixing plus a mana sink. 55.1% GIH; fine in UW/UR/GU vehicle shells, marginal outside them.
Riverpyre Verge: Solid fixing for UR. A dual that taps for R or U once you control an Island or Mountain — reliable untapped fixing that any Izzet cycling/spells deck wants. The 54.6% GIH and +1.2 IWD are strong for a land; take it on-color, and it enables splashing the format's good uncommons.
Rocky Roads: Niche RW/vehicles land, a role-player. Enters untapped only with a Mount/Vehicle out and can sac for a Pilot token to crew — cute in Boros but the -2.2 IWD flags it as a tempo tax that comes in tapped early. C+ grade is generous; only play it in a dedicated crew deck.
Rugged Highlands: Standard tapland fixing for RG (or a red/green splash). Enters tapped with a 1-life gift; the tempo cost is real but negligible in this slow format where mana consistency wins grindy games. 54.5% GIH reflects the fixing premium — take it to smooth a two-color or splash deck, not as a pick priority.
Scoured Barrens: Playable fixing for WB/Mardu. Same tapland-plus-1-life package for white-black; useful for two-color consistency or a light splash in this grindy format where tapping out on turn one costs little. 55.1% GIH and 55% play rate reflect its role as a fixer, not a card you prioritize.
Sunbillow Verge: Solid fixing, run it in any RW deck. A rare dual that enters untapped-capable, tapping for W or R once you control a Mountain or Plains — better than a tapland when your basics cooperate. 52.6% GIH matches the C+; unglamorous but real mana-fixing that helps the demanding RW/aggro manabases, take it over marginal spells.
Swiftwater Cliffs: Standard tapland fixing — take it when you're UR or splashing. The lifegain softens the enters-tapped cost and it fixes the UR cycling deck's colors; 55% GIH / +1.5 IWD is normal dual-land value, mostly a deck-smoothing pick. Grab it mid-to-late when your manabase needs it, not over playables.
Thornwood Falls: Playable fixing for GU decks — same story as the other taplands. Slow format forgives the tapped land, the lifegain buffers, and it enables green splashes; 56.2% GIH and 66.9% play. Take it to fix and splash, prioritize it below actual spells. C+ is right.
Tranquil Cove: Solid fixing and a fine mid-pack pick — a tapland that gains 1 life and fixes WU, the kind of glue that quietly wins the grindy games this format produces. 55.3% GIH and a healthy +2.0 IWD earn the C+; grab it to enable WU/Esper splashes or any two-color white-blue deck. The life matters more than usual in a slow format.
Wastewood Verge: A rare BG dual that fixes untapped — taps for G or B as long as you control a Swamp or Forest, so it's strictly better than the tapland once you're base-green or -black. The 55.4% GIH and early 3.8 ALSA reflect its value to BG, the best archetype. Prioritize it in any black-green deck; excellent fixing with no tempo cost.
Wild Roads: Solid fixing with upside for green/vehicle decks. Enters untapped if you have a Mount/Vehicle, taps for {G}, and late sacs into a 1/1 Pilot that crews/saddles like power 2 — real crew fixing that never sits dead. 55.4% GIH and 62% play rate beat the C+ grade; a fine early-mid pick in RW/GU vehicle shells.
Willowrush Verge: Excellent GU fixing land, effectively free to run. Untapped dual that fixes UG cleanly with a trivial Forest/Island condition, boosting consistency in the exhaust/ramp GU decks. 55.8% GIH and +1.9 IWD; prioritize when in blue-green, and take over marginal playables for the mana.
Wind-Scarred Crag: Standard dual land — playable fixing, not a pick priority. Enters tapped, gains 1 life, taps for {R} or {W}; take it to enable RW or a splash. 52.6% GIH is just the cost of the tapland; grab it in the fixing rounds, never over a real card.
Cavalier of Dawn: Bomb, take it early (data-based — card text is missing here). The 61.6% GIH, +8.6 IWD and 2.3 ALSA all point to a game-ending white five-drop that overperforms; provisional on the oracle text but the numbers are unambiguous. Slam it in any white deck and let it anchor big-white midrange.
Thoughtcast: Solid card advantage for UB/UR artifact decks. Affinity-for-artifacts makes it a one-or-two-mana draw-two in the affinity shell — cheap fuel and card flow. The 49.7% GIH (no OH data, no CGB) is dragged by decks casting it at full price; in an artifact-dense build it's an efficient enabler, provisional read.
Whir of Invention: No data (null GIH, 12.7% play rate) so read is provisional. It's an artifact tutor-to-battlefield with convoke — a build-around that only earns a slot if you have specific artifact targets worth cheating out, and the tiny play rate says drafters rarely did. Treat as a niche combo enabler; likely sideboard filler in most UR/artifact pools.
Bone Miser: Provisional read — data is thin and the tile lacks text/grade. Bone Miser is a discard-payoff rare (mana/cards/creatures off discards) that needs a discard-matters shell (UR cycling, BR) to shine and is near-blank otherwise. The 46.9% GIH and -1.1 IWD suggest it underdelivered outside that build; treat as a niche build-around, low pick unless your deck actively discards.
Lord of the Undead: Role-player, provisional read with incomplete data. A zombie lord in a set light on tribal payoff, so its ceiling depends on picking up enough zombies/embalm bodies in WB or UB. The middling 50.1% GIH, -3.8 IWD and null OH/grade suggest it underdelivers as a standalone; take it as a synergy piece, not a bomb.
Chandra's Ignition: Strong red rare — the null grade is just missing data, but the live 57.3% GIH / +5.1 IWD and 2.6 ALSA say take it high. Pointed at a big creature it's a one-sided sweeper that clears the board and burns the opponent, exactly the catch-up tool this slow format rewards. Provisional on the exact text, but the numbers are a clear buy.
Galvanic Blast: Efficient red burn — high pick, and the null grade is just missing data, not a knock. Cheap instant removal/reach is exactly what this grindy format wants, and in an artifact-heavy deck it can deal 4; 54.8% GIH with +1.6 IWD and 3.6 ALSA. Provisional on the grade, but treat cheap red removal as a strong maindeck card in any red build.
Pathbreaker Ibex: Strong green rare and a high pick — the classic mini-Overrun that pumps your whole team by the greatest power among your creatures and grants trample, a devastating alpha-strike finisher for the go-big green decks. 57.3% GIH with a 2.2 ALSA and 89% play rate confirm it's a reliable bomb-adjacent closer; card data was null but the effect is well-known. Prioritize in any green stompy build.
Chrome Mox: Null-data mythic — read is provisional. Imprint a colored card for a free artifact mana rock; in a slow, grindy Limited format the card disadvantage and inconsistency make it a niche accelerant, not a slam. The 3.1 ALSA shows people take it speculatively, but without WR data treat it as a low-priority pick unless you're an aggressive or fixing-hungry deck.
Skysovereign, Consul Flagship: Colorless bomb, near-unconditional first pick. A flying Vehicle that deals 3 to a creature or planeswalker on ETB and again each attack — repeatable removal on an evasive threat that any deck can play. 66.2% GIH, +12.7 IWD, ALSA 1.1 and a 100% play rate say it all. Take it and build around it.
